label: Climate & disturbance
blurb: Recent fire, projected climate exposure and sea-level rise: how much of the 30x30 network they touch, and how much of each lies in 30x30.

headlines.label: 30x30 network in 5 ft sea-level rise zone

charts.title: Climate and disturbance features
charts.subtitle: Share of each feature's extent in this area by conservation status

method: Burned area is every CAL FIRE fire perimeter from 2015 on (the report's 'past decade'), on resolution-10 cells; statewide this gives 13.9% of the 30x30 network burned (report: 14%). Climate exposure is Thorne et al. (2016) for mid-century, natural vegetation only (CWHR major-habitat classes other than agriculture and urban), with an exposure index of 0.95 or more counted as exposed, separately for the MIROC5 and CNRM-CM5 models; statewide, 32.2% of MIROC5-exposed natural vegetation lies in 30x30 (the report's draft analysis: 31.7%). The report's prose says 32% of the network's natural vegetation is projected to be stressed; this app computes about 22% of the network for either model, and has not reproduced the 32% figure. Sea-level rise is NOAA's 5-foot inundation layer, which includes existing open water and so does not match the report's extent (tracked in ca-30x30#104). The report publishes no need classes for these features.
